title: Polylogarithmic depth under DAG conversion
statement: Let $C$ be a family of Boolean circuits indexed by input length, and let $d$ be a natural number. If there is a natural number $b$ such that, for every $n$, the depth of the circuit $C_n$ is at most $b(\log_2 n+1)^d$, then the family of directed acyclic graph circuits obtained from $C$ satisfies the same depth bound with some natural-number constant.
hypotheses_covered: A family C of tree circuits
There exists a natural-number bound b for which every input length n has depth at most b times (log₂ n + 1)^d
